clue.text: Staff in the money make a mockery of it

indicators.note: the staff word is placed inside the money word, as the clue says one goes in the other

parts.note: pay is the money a worker receives
a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: Someone with a stick among the cash makes fun of the whole thing.
explanation.definitionFit: To lampoon something by comic imitation is to mock it.

clue.text: A number of buttons

parts.note: reads as a count of fasteners, but Buttons is the pantomime pageboy's name, so several of them are boy servants; also a book's leaves are numbered

explanation.walkthrough: Buttons is the pageboy in the British pantomime Cinderella, and uniformed boy attendants were nicknamed buttons for their brass-buttoned jackets.
explanation.definitionFit: Buttons is the traditional name for a uniformed boy servant, so several such boys are young attendants.

clue.text: Dependable follower of Robin

explanation.walkthrough: The Reliant Robin is a famous British three-wheeled car; the surface suggests one of Robin Hood's band.
explanation.definitionFit: Dependable means trustworthy; the Reliant Robin was a British three-wheeled car, so the maker's name sits before Robin.

clue.text: Warship found in ancient battle-site amid tangled reeds

indicators.note: the battle-site sits in the middle of the jumbled reeds, as amid says
tangled reeds are knotted together, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: Troy was the site of the Trojan War in ancient legend

explanation.surface: A naval vessel discovered at a classical battlefield among knotted reeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tangled' turns REEDS into DESER, and 'amid' puts TROY inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A destroyer is a fast naval fighting vessel, a kind of warship.

clue.text: Quietly humorous nonsense that brings the house down

parts.note: dry humour is understated and deadpan
rot is rubbish or nonsense

explanation.surface: A deadpan comedian's silliness brings the house down with laughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Fungal decay of timber can make a building collapse.

clue.text: Way out secured by sappers

indicators.note: the word out is held in place inside the sappers' letters

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are the British army's sappers
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exit route protected by military engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: A route is a road or path to follow.

clue.text: They may work in cutting variety of mineral

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Miners in a quarry working through different kinds of rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway cutting is a trench dug for track, where railway workers may be found.

clue.text: Learn to reform and the church shows compassion

indicators.note: to reform is to reshape, so the letters of the two words are reshaped

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Learning to change and the church's display of mercy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' rearranges LEARN TO into TOLERAN, then CE follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Forbearance and sympathy towards others are close in sense, as is patient understanding.

clue.text: Classic way to appear more youthful?

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into two words: age less.
explanation.definitionFit: Classic means timeless; read as two words, to age less is to look younger.

clue.text: Final services of Airbus reviewed around end of April

indicators.note: the reworked plane name goes round the single letter
reviewed suggests looking over again, here reshaping the letters
end of picks the closing letter of the month

explanation.surface: An aircraft maker's last maintenance checks, revisited near late spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewed' turns AIRBUS into BURIAS, and 'around' wraps it round L.
explanation.definitionFit: Funerals are the last rites given to the dead.

clue.text: What the stars did? Mostly made rubbish!

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition works on the answer without its first letter: LITTERED means made rubbish, so 'Mostly' tells you to cut the G.
explanation.definitionFit: Stars twinkled and sparkled; most of the word, dropping its first letter, means strewn with litter.

clue.text: It's made solely of rope

parts.note: solely sounds like only, but means the sole of the shoe is woven from rope or jute

explanation.definitionFit: This canvas shoe traditionally has a sole of plaited rope or jute.

clue.text: She's no right to take a husband

indicators.note: no right means the right letter is removed from the word

parts.note: to marry is to take a spouse

explanation.surface: A woman with no entitlement to wed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' takes one R out of MARRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, so a female person stands for it.

clue.text: Crazy instruction the young must sit through

parts.note: potty is British slang for mad
training is teaching or instruction

explanation.surface: Mad lessons that children have to sit through.
explanation.definitionFit: Toddlers learn to use a chamber pot, literally sitting through the lessons.

clue.text: Indicates trouble for Railtrack

explanation.walkthrough: Railtrack ran Britain's rail infrastructure; points are the movable rails at a junction, and points being out of order delay trains.
explanation.definitionFit: Indicates means shows; railway switches failing is trouble for a rail operator.

clue.text: See 13
Errant husband may be due later, right!

indicators.note: may be signals the letters could become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A wayward spouse might be home late, true enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' rearranges DUE LATER into ADULTERE, then R ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheating spouse is one unfaithful to their marriage.

clue.text: Ex-Spice Girl joins queue for clothing department

indicators.note: the singer joins the queue by stepping into it

parts.note: a line is a queue
Geri Halliwell left the Spice Girls pop group

explanation.surface: A former pop star queues up in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spice Girls were a 1990s British pop group; Geri Halliwell famously left it.
explanation.definitionFit: Women's underwear is sold in its own section of a department store.

clue.text: Working girl came top, yet given third degree

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: to come top is to lead, so led

explanation.surface: A girl with a job who finished first and then was interrogated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' rearranges GIRL into GRIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Questioned intensely, as the police do in an interrogation.

clue.text: Pawnbroker's soiled article finally disposed of

indicators.note: the article at the end of the word is thrown away

parts.note: soiled means dirty
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A pawnbroker's dirty item finally got rid of.
explanation.walkthrough: Uncle is old British slang for a pawnbroker.
explanation.definitionFit: Old slang names a moneylender who takes goods in pledge after a relative.

clue.text: Vehicles without a home at times

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the vehicles go round the letter

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Homeless people sometimes live in vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vehicles' gives two, a car and a van, and 'without' means outside here, so they surround A.
explanation.definitionFit: A mobile trailer serves as a dwelling on holiday.

clue.text: Some free tuition given in this case

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Lessons provided at no charge in this situation.
explanation.definitionFit: A small ornamental needle case, so a holder for small items.

clue.text: Kind of recorder played in Scottish dance sequence

explanation.walkthrough: A reel is a Scottish country dance as well as a tape spool.
explanation.definitionFit: An old tape machine running between two spools; also a string of lively Scottish dances one after another.

clue.text: Turner displayed upside down — who can tell?

indicators.text: displayed upside down — who can tell?
indicators.note: reading the word backwards makes no difference, so nobody could tell

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A Turner painting hung the wrong way up and nobody notices.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating part of a machine is something that spins.

clue.text: Follow directions before use, stupid!

parts.note: E and N are compass directions, east and north

indicators.note: stupid suggests the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: Read the instructions before use, you fool!
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupid' rearranges USE into SUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To result or come after is to occur next.

clue.text: T.S. Eliot's letters edited for ladies

indicators.note: editing changes text, so the poet's name letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A poet's correspondence revised for female readers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ladies' is the British word for women's lavatories.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladies is a common sign for women's public conveniences.

clue.text: Most daring items of underwear

parts.note: a bra is an undergarment
a vest is a British undergarment, a sleeveless undershirt

explanation.surface: The boldest pieces of lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a vest is an undershirt, not a waistcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: The most courageous person is the boldest one.

clue.text: Doctor Stroud's house

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A physician named Stroud and his home.
explanation.walkthrough: Stroud is a town in Gloucestershire; the house is a royal dynasty, not a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A royal house is a dynasty, and this was the English royal family from 1485 to 1603.

clue.text: Possibly Emily's little brother's turned ten

parts.note: bro is short for brother

indicators.note: turned suggests the letters are twisted into another order

explanation.surface: Emily's younger sibling has had his tenth birthday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' rearranges TEN into NTE; Emily Brontë wrote Wuthering Heights.
explanation.definitionFit: Emily was one of three famous novelist sisters of that surname.
